bottleneck: KYC binds an enrolled legal entity but does not by itself prioritize separately KYC'd entities that may coordinate repeated probes.
hypothesis: A low-authority behavior score can prioritize common-controller credential pairs for review at a calibrated one-percent false-positive cap without changing KYC identity or access automatically.
prediction: Held-out synthetic pair AUC will be 0.85.
likely_failure: Independent legal entities following the same trading strategy produce high similarity and reduce precision.
single_change: Add an interpretable behavior similarity score and calibrate only its human-review threshold on a population disjoint from evaluation.
baseline: KYC-only control with no behavior-prioritized review queue
evaluation_population: Two disjoint seeded synthetic populations of 80 controllers with separately KYC'd common-controller positives
rejection_rule: Reject the point prediction if held-out AUC is below 0.75 or test false-positive rate exceeds 0.02; all synthetic results remain smoke_only.
promotion_rule: Behavior cannot merge entities or deny service, and this run cannot support production use before externally labeled validation.
new_causal_evidence: The recorded command names a file that no longer exists. The measurement instrument was reimplemented in Rust and the Python it invoked was deleted, so the receipt on QOMM-ENTITY-BEHAVIOR-SMOKE-001 describes a run of a different instrument than the one this repository now contains. The Rust binary was compared against that Python value by value while both existed --- 26 non-timing values identical, 0 different --- so this is a re-run of the same experiment on a rebuilt instrument, not a new hypothesis. Nothing about the market, the seeds, the population or the rules has changed.
